title: Instance validation: badf_gate.py instance <path> and a per-instance lockfile
objective: Make a project's badf/ governed rather than decorative: one command validates the instance's documents, corroborates them against each other and against git (instance baseline, framework revision), and verifies a per-instance lockfile written by init.
business_value: An instance nobody reads is a claim nobody checks. Validation is what lets a later work package advance state.json through governed transitions and refuse a hand-typed one.
in_scope: badf/lockfile.json in the instance, written by init, same implementation as the framework's (lock/verify parameterised by root and patterns)
tests in scratch instances; mutation; post-merge simulation
out_of_scope: any run against a real project
acceptance_criteria: a hand-edited state.json is refused (lockfile drift) and, if re-signed, refused on cross-document disagreement
a receipt or state naming a baseline commit the instance does not have, or that is not an ancestor of HEAD, is refused
a framework_revision unknown to this framework is refused
the framework itself is refused as an instance
a preserved AGENTS.md that changed since baseline is reported, not refused
the framework's own lock/verify behaviour is unchanged (existing integrity tests green)
permissions: write: scratch repositories under the test tmpdir only
evidence: mutation on the corroboration checks, unique anchors
post-merge simulation cited in the PR

rollback.method: revert the squash commit via PR

note: Lands IN_PROGRESS by design; reconciled by the next WP's branch.
